questions.question: What is the main non-renewable resource used to manufacture most traditional plastic food packaging?
options: Crude oil and fossil fuels
Wood pulp and timber
Corn starch and biomass
Silicon and sand

questions.question: Why is plastic waste in oceans and landfills considered a major environmental pollutant?
options: It degrades instantly into toxic gases
It takes a very long time to break down and can injure wildlife
It dissolves in water and makes oceans highly acidic
It prevents solar radiation from reaching the Earth's surface

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a sustainable alternative to traditional fossil-fuel-based plastic packaging?
options: Chlorinated PVC wrapping
Single-use polystyrene containers
Biodegradable bioplastics made from renewable resources
Heavy-duty metal alloy foil

questions.question: What is a key benefit of using plastic packaging for food products?
options: It speeds up the ripening process of fruits
It helps prevent food spoilage and reduces food waste
It completely eliminates the need for refrigeration
It increases the nutritional value of the food inside

questions.question: What is one of the primary drivers of global deforestation today?
options: Clearing land to grow crops and raise livestock
Building solar panel farms in rural areas
Harvesting wild berries and mushrooms
Creating national parks for conservation

questions.question: What is a direct consequence of deforestation on forest-dwelling species?
options: An increase in available nesting sites
Rapid adaptation to urban environments
Habitat loss and destruction of their natural homes
An immediate rise in population sizes

questions.question: Which of the following is a land-based mitigation strategy to combat climate change and biodiversity loss?
options: Paving over grasslands for urban development
Reforestation and rewilding of natural areas
Expanding monoculture crop production
Increasing the use of synthetic pesticides

questions.question: How does climate change directly make global food production more difficult and unpredictable?
options: By decreasing the rate of weed growth
By making extreme weather events more common
By permanently blocking all sunlight from crops
By turning all freshwater into saltwater

questions.question: What determines the overall carbon footprint of a food product?
options: Only the distance the food travels in delivery vans
The amount of water used to wash the food after harvest
Greenhouse gas emissions from all stages of its production
The total weight of the plastic packaging used

questions.question: Why does clearing forests disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: Fewer trees are available to absorb carbon dioxide for photosynthesis
It stops plants from releasing oxygen during respiration
It increases the rate at which trees absorb nitrogen from the soil
It prevents carbon dioxide from dissolving into rainwater

questions.question: What role does carbon dioxide (CO2) play in the atmosphere?
options: It destroys ozone to let more UV rays cool the earth
It is a greenhouse gas that enhances the greenhouse effect and drives climate change
It acts as a cooling agent that prevents solar radiation from warming land
It directly neutralizes other harmful industrial air pollutants

questions.question: How does the removal of trees during deforestation disrupt the water cycle?
options: It increases the rate of transpiration into the atmosphere
It stops clouds from releasing rainfall entirely
Less water is absorbed by roots and transpired by leaves
It causes all groundwater to instantly evaporate

questions.question: Why does deforestation increase the risk of flooding and threaten food security?
options: It leads to more surface runoff of rainwater instead of absorption
It causes rivers to dry up instantly due to lack of shade
It decreases the amount of rainfall in mountainous regions
It makes soils too compact to hold any surface water

questions.question: How does climate change affect species that have evolved specific adaptations for their habitats?
options: It instantly gives them new adaptations to survive anywhere
It alters habitat conditions, making species less well-suited to their environment
It ensures that their food supplies will always increase
It eliminates all competing species in their ecosystem

questions.question: How do some species successfully cope with changing conditions in their native habitats?
options: By instantly mutating to breathe underwater
By migrating to a new, more suitable habitat
By entering a permanent state of hibernation
By changing their diet to consume non-living matter
